questions.question: What is the first physical unit produced by blocked index construction?
options: A sorted immutable run built within a memory budget
One globally mutable postings file updated randomly
A dense term-document matrix for the full corpus
A query-specific ranking generated before tokenization

questions.question: In what order are occurrence records sorted?
options: Worker, arrival time, random key
Term, document ID, position
Position, document length, filename

questions.topic: Blocked Index Construction: Build Runs, Merge Runs
questions.question: Why should workers use deterministic document IDs?
options: Local counters always coordinate globally without communication
Document IDs are removed before postings are merged
Different IDs improve detection of the same source document
Independent counters can collide or make replays produce different postings

questions.topic: Blocked Index Construction: Build Runs, Merge Runs
questions.question: What makes an immutable run useful for failure recovery?
options: A committed checksum-validated run can be reused by a retry
Readers can consume it safely while its bytes are still changing
It eliminates the need to record input scope or analyzer version
A partial write is automatically equivalent to a complete run

questions.topic: Blocked Index Construction: Build Runs, Merge Runs
questions.question: Why should final validation reconcile source and index counts?
options: A readable dictionary proves every input block was included
A structurally valid index can still omit a completed source scope
Postings counts are unrelated to construction completeness
Checksums guarantee that rejected documents were indexed

questions.question: What triggers a logarithmic merge to the next level?
options: A query contains more than one term
A document receives a new relevance score
A new segment collides with an occupied segment at its size level
A reader opens the current manifest

questions.question: With geometrically sized levels, how many occupied segments exist in the simple model?
options: O(N squared)
Exactly N
O(sqrt N)
O(log N)

questions.question: Base batch size is 1,000. What happens when the fourth batch arrives after two batches already formed level 1 and batch three occupies level 0?
options: Level 0 merges to level 1, then carries into a 4,000-document level 2
All four batches remain independent at level 0 forever
The first three batches are deleted and only batch four remains
Every source document is rebuilt under a new analyzer

questions.question: How are deletes represented before a merge removes old postings physically?
options: As negative document frequencies in every dictionary
As tombstones that suppress older document versions
As random changes to compressed document-ID gaps
As query terms added to every live document

questions.question: Why must a merge commit use a generation-aware manifest?
options: To block every new document until all readers terminate
To overwrite newer segments that arrived after the merge snapshot
To replace merged inputs while preserving segments created concurrently
To expose the new segment before its output is durable

questions.question: What is the main cost of delaying background merges too long?
options: Source documents become impossible to tokenize
Stable document IDs change on every query
All index writes become globally transactional
Segment fan-out, stale bytes, and query work accumulate

questions.topic: Rebuild vs Merge: Index Update Strategy Tradeoffs
questions.question: What is a major correctness benefit of a full rebuild?
options: It re-derives coherent state from the authoritative corpus
It always provides lower update latency than a small segment
It avoids reading source documents or analyzer configuration
It preserves every historical tombstone and obsolete posting

questions.topic: Rebuild vs Merge: Index Update Strategy Tradeoffs
questions.question: What is a major benefit of incremental merging?
options: It removes all segment and version-management complexity
It incorporates small changes without rewriting the complete corpus
It guarantees old analyzer generations remain compatible
It makes periodic reconciliation unnecessary

questions.topic: Rebuild vs Merge: Index Update Strategy Tradeoffs
questions.question: A 50,000-document policy corpus changes weekly and rebuilds in four minutes. Which choice is strongest?
options: Permanent complex merge machinery regardless of operational cost
One mutable postings file edited randomly during serving
Simple versioned full replacement with validation
Never updating the index because the corpus is small

questions.topic: Rebuild vs Merge: Index Update Strategy Tradeoffs
questions.question: Why does a new tokenizer generally require a complete new index version?
options: Tokenization changes only display text after retrieval
Old postings can infer every new token boundary without source text
Mixed analyzers guarantee identical term statistics
The analyzer changes keys, postings, positions, and ranking statistics

questions.topic: Rebuild vs Merge: Index Update Strategy Tradeoffs
questions.question: When can a large deletion wave favor rebuilding?
options: When emitting only live data is cheaper than carrying many tombstones through merges
When no source-of-truth record identifies which documents remain live
When deletion must keep all obsolete postings query-visible
When rebuild output cannot be versioned or atomically published

questions.topic: Rebuild vs Merge: Index Update Strategy Tradeoffs
questions.question: What hybrid policy balances freshness and drift control?
options: Full rebuild after every document and no incremental segments
Incremental segments and merges plus periodic reconciliation or rebuild
Unlimited segments with no compaction or source comparison
In-place file mutation without manifests or rollback versions
